title: The Future of Evals - Ankur Goyal, Braintrust
talk_summary: Braintrust's Ankur Goyal recaps that evals to date are manual dashboards, then demos 'Loop', an agent that automatically optimizes prompts, datasets, and scorers inside Braintrust. He claims frontier models only recently became good at this, with Claude 4 performing ~6x better than the prior leading model at improving prompts/datasets/scorers.

takeaways.technique: Agent-driven eval artifact optimization (prompts, datasets, scorers)
takeaways.what_they_do: An agent proposes edits to prompts, new scoring ideas, and dataset changes, shown side-by-side in the UI for human review, with an optional 'just go for it' autonomous mode.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it can automatically optimize uh your prompts all the way to very complex uh agents ... it also helps you build better data sets and better scorers
takeaways.numbers: Claude 4 performs almost 6x better than the previous leading model at improving prompts/datasets/scorers

takeaways.technique: Evals as the gate for model/prompt changes
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat prompt, dataset, and scorer as a triad that must be evaluated together, and they benchmark frontier models quarterly on the task of improving those artifacts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's really the combination of these three things that make for really great evals

takeaways.technique: Quarterly frontier-model capability benchmarking for meta-tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Every quarter they re-run evals on frontier models to see how good they are at improving prompts, datasets, and scorers, rather than assuming a fixed ranking.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Every quarter for the last two years, we've run evals on the frontier models to see how good they are at actually improving prompts

takeaways.technique: Human-in-the-loop vs autonomous toggle for optimization agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Loop defaults to surfacing suggested edits side-by-side for review, with an opt-in 'just go for it' mode for autonomous optimization.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's also a toggle that you can turn on that says like just go for it and it will go and optimize away
